pr.title: Open a spec's pull request and ask the user to review the plan
pr.head: eac08a032c010f35797165681f05193a8e3d21a4

summary: Projector's spec skill writes a project's plan under docs/projects/. A plan's decisions belong to the user, so the user reads every plan before anyone builds it. Before this change, spec left the plan uncommitted unless asked, and when it did open a pull request it marked it ready at once. Marking a pull request ready is what starts Projector's automated review, so that review read a design the user was about to change.

After this change, spec commits the plan on a branch, opens a draft pull request, subscribes the session to fix it, and posts one inbox request asking the user to review the plan as GitHub renders it. The pull request stays a draft until the user answers:

• Looks good or a decline: spec runs project review ready.
  • Some feedback: spec revises the plan, pushes, and revises the same request.
  • A question only the user can answer goes out first as an ask, before the review request.
  • Without the inbox tools, spec marks the pull request ready at the hand-over.

Several other places state the rule that a pull request stays a draft while a test request waits on the user. Each widens one sentence to cover a plan review request too, so fix-pr, work, and cleanup never mark a plan's pull request ready behind the user's back.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Draft: a GitHub pull request state that says its author is still working. A session that reviews the repository waits for it to be marked ready.
  • Inbox: Projector's panel above the user's prompt, where ask, tell, and request items wait until answered.
  • Generated section: the Projector conventions block that project init writes into a repository's AGENTS.md, versioned by its begin marker.

groups.title: The spec skill's new hand-over
groups.kicker: How spec opens the plan's pull request and asks the user to review it
intro: The Validate and hand over section of skills/spec/SKILL.md now ends with two subsections. Open the pull request commits the plan on a branch, checks the whole branch with a range git diff --check, pushes, opens a draft pull request, and subscribes the session. Ask the user to review the plan settles blocking questions with ask, posts one review request, and acts on the answer.

files.note: The whole new flow: opening the draft, the review request's fields, and what each answer does.

checks.text: The bare git diff --check earlier in the section reads only tracked working-tree changes, so it misses a new plan file. The range form against the default branch reads the whole branch.
A spec run that only pushes a refinement to an existing pull request posts no request, because the session that opened that pull request holds its draft state.

project review ready reports that a pull request is already ready rather than failing, so Looks good after an automated-review-first hand-over is harmless. Checked in set_draft in src/projector/review.py.

groups.title: The draft-hold rule, widened
groups.kicker: Every place that keeps a tested pull request a draft now keeps a plan's too
intro: implement keeps a pull request a draft while a device-test request waits on the user. Other skills and the generated section restate that rule so they never mark such a pull request ready. Each restatement widens one sentence to cover a request to review a plan.

checks.text: The generated block in AGENTS.md is byte-identical to the template with {projects_dir} rendered as docs/projects. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md.

files.note: Version 26 of the generated section: names spec's hand-over and widens the draft rule.
The repository's own hand-over rule widened, and the generated section refreshed to version 26.
Under Report the result: a draft spec keeps for a plan review is not fix-pr's to mark ready.
Keeps a plan's pull request a draft until the user answers its review request.

checks.text: The sentence names both hand-overs that keep a pull request a draft: ../implement/SKILL.md for a test request and ../spec/SKILL.md for a plan review request. Both paths resolve from skills/work/, and each file describes its hold.

files.note: Counts a draft kept for a test or plan review request as a held pull request, which cleanup marks ready when the user leaves it.

groups.title: Plan, documentation, and tests
groups.kicker: The plan's outcome, the plugin docs, and the two pinned tests
intro: The plan is marked completed with a new § 7 that records what shipped. docs/plugins.md describes the new hand-over. Two tests guard the change: one pins the generated section's version 26 hash, and one now also checks that spec runs no bare gh pr ready in a command block.

files.note: Status moves to completed; § 7 Outcome records the evidence.
